articles.title: One suspect killed as vigilantes foil terrorist attack on Kwara community
articles.description: One suspected terrorist has been killed after local vigilantes repelled an attempted attack on Nanu community in Kaiama local government area of Kwara state. The incident reportedly occurred around 3:30am on Wednesday when armed men attempted to invade the community. Zagazola Makama, a security-focused publication, reports that troops of the 22 brigade stationed at the forward pperating base in Kaiama responded to intelligence about the planned assault. The security personnel, alongside local vigilantes, reportedly engaged the attackers, disrupting their advance and forcing them to withdraw. One of the suspected terrorists was killed during the confrontation, while the others fled. The incident adds to a series of attacks targeting communities and security formations in Kaiama, one of the areas facing persistent security threats in northern Kwara. On February 3, suspected terrorists attacked Nuku and Woro communities in the LGA, killing at least 75 residents and setting several houses ablaze. About 150 people, mostly women and children, were also abducted. The victims were released in August after six months in captivity. The attack, which drew widespread condemnation, prompted President Bola Tinubu to approve the deployment of an army battalion to the area under Operation Savannah Shield. On April 20, suspected terrorists attacked another community in Kaiama, killing three soldiers. The attackers reportedly attempted to overrun the facility but were repelled by troops. Barely two weeks later, on May 2, gunmen attacked a police mobile force camp in Tenebo, Kaiama, killing three police officers and injuring several others. Following the Wednesday attack, troops are expected to sustain operations in the area to prevent further attacks and track down the fleeing assailants.
